name: Naming Convention Enforcer
blurb: nets, symbols, parts and files checked against one naming rule
intro: Paste names one per line; each is checked against one case rule plus the rules for its kind (IEEE 315 class letters for reference designators, portable characters for files, 3V3-style values for nets), with a suggested rename. Names that differ only in case or separators are flagged: tools disagree on whether they are the same.

usage: Give names as one per line in names (optionally prefixed net:, ref:, part: or file:), the kind (auto, net, refdes, part, file), the case style (upper_snake, lower_snake, kebab, camel, pascal or custom with pattern as a regex), maxlen in characters (0 = none) and optional comma-separated prefixes. It returns pass/fail counts, a failures table with the problem and a suggested name, clashes between names that differ only in case or separators, and a CSV rename map. Use it before a netlist review, a library cleanup or a file release.
sources: IEEE 315-1975 / ASME Y14.44-2008 reference designator class letters
IEEE 1003.1 (POSIX) portable filename character set, section 3.282
Microsoft: Naming Files, Paths, and Namespaces (reserved device names)
Case styles: convention, not a standard
